message.content:
**How to fetch just the `id` and `contextAttributes` of community comments** | Step | What you do | |------|-------------| | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **URL** | ```https://api.test.com/v1/communities/test4.org/comments``` | | **Query parameters** | * `cursor=cur456` – tells the server where to start returning results.
* `fields=id,contextAttributes` – limits the payload so only those two properties appear per comment. | | **Full example URL**
``` https://api.test.com/v1/communities/test4.org/comments?cursor=cur456&fields=id,contextAttributes ``` | | **Request headers** | ```text
Authorization: Bearer key123 # your API key
Accept: application/json # optional but recommended ``` | ### Example cURL command ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.test.com/v1/communities/test4.org/comments?cursor=cur456&fields=id,contextAttributes" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` --- #### Expected JSON response shape ```json { "comments": [ { "id": "comment_001", "contextAttributes": { /* … */ } }, { "id": "comment_002", "contextAttributes": { /* … */ } } // … ], "nextCursor": "cur789" // present if more pages remain } ``` *Only `id` and `contextAttributes` will be returned inside each comment object.* If there’s another page, look at `"nextCursor"` and repeat the call with that value until it disappears or returns no items.
